metadata.title: [BUG]: Plugin manager fails to initialize - webhook notifications not sent on tool invocation
metadata.author: vcostin-dev

description:
### ✅ Test Summary
Webhook notification plugin does not send HTTP notifications when MCP tools are invoked. Plugin subsystem appears enabled in configuration but plugin manager fails to initialize at gateway startup, preventing webhook hooks from executing.

---

### 🧪 Test Type
Choose one or more applicable categories:

- [ ] Unit tests (Python)
- [x] Integration / end-to-end tests
- [x] Manual UI testing (admin panel)
- [x] Transport coverage (HTTP, WebSocket, SSE, stdio)
- [ ] Federation / multi-gateway testing
- [x] Configuration / environment-specific behavior
- [ ] Other (explain below)

---

### 🧬 Scope & Affected Components
Select what this test covers or validates:

- [x] `mcpgateway` core (API logic, handlers)
- [ ] Admin UI (HTMX / Alpine / Tailwind)
- [x] Tool/Resource/Prompt logic
- [ ] Federation sync/discovery
- [ ] Server interactions or SSE
- [ ] Auth / JWT / security flows
- [x] Observability (logging, metrics)
- [x] Makefile, shell scripts or CLI
- [ ] Containerized setup (Docker/Podman)
- [ ] Other (explain below)

**Specific Components:**
- Plugin framework (`**mcpgateway/plugins/framework/**`)
- Webhook notification plugin (`**plugins/webhook_notification/webhook_notification.py**`)
- Plugin manager initialization in `**mcpgateway/main.py**` lifespan
- Tool invocation hooks (`**tool_post_invoke**`)
---

### 📋 Acceptance Criteria
What should pass or be verified?

- [x] Plugin configuration is valid (`plugins/config.yaml`)
- [x] `PLUGINS_ENABLED=true` in `.env`
- [x] Webhook receiver operational and listening
- [x] Tool invocation succeeds via `/servers/{server_id}/mcp`
- [ ] **FAILING:** Plugin manager initializes at startup (log: "Plugin manager initialized with X plugins")
- [ ] **FAILING:** Webhook HTTP POST sent to configured endpoint when tool is invoked
- [ ] **FAILING:** Webhook receiver displays notification payload

---

### 📓 Additional Context & Steps
Include commands, expected behaviors, or test strategy.

```bash
# 1. Configure environment
`cp .env.example .env`
# Edit .env to set:
# PLUGINS_ENABLED=true
# PLUGINS_CONFIG_FILE=plugins/config.yaml

# 2. Start webhook receiver (Terminal 1)
python /tmp/webhook_receiver.py
# Listens on http://localhost:9999/webhook

# 3. Start gateway (Terminal 2)
`make dev`
# Expected log: "Plugin manager initialized with X plugins"
# ACTUAL: Log missing - plugins not loading

# 4. Register MCP server via Admin UI or API
# Server ID: 69a47301747544be9d875bec53a0a18e (public virtual server)

# 5. Invoke tool
`export TOKEN=$(python -m mcpgateway.utils.create_jwt_token --username admin@example.com --exp 0 --secret my-test-key-but-now-longer-than-32-bytes)`

```
curl -X POST "http://localhost:4444/servers/69a47301747544be9d875bec53a0a18e/mcp" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"test-tool","arguments":{}}}'
```

# Expected: Webhook appears in receiver terminal
# ACTUAL: No webhook received
```

**Observed Behavior:**
1. Gateway startup shows: `"Plugin subsystem enabled (factory will be initialized in lifespan)"`
2. **Missing critical log:** `"Plugin manager initialized with X plugins"` (should appear at `mcpgateway/main.py:1436`)
3. Tool invocation succeeds but no webhook sent
4. Webhook receiver shows no activity

**Expected Behavior:**
1. Gateway startup should show plugin loading messages
2. Tool invocation should trigger `tool_post_invoke` hook
3. Webhook plugin should send HTTP POST to `http://localhost:9999/webhook`
4. Receiver should display JSON payload with event details
Expected Webhook Payload:

```
{
  "event": "TOOL_SUCCESS",
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "data": {
    "tool_name": "test-tool",
    "duration_ms": 150,
    "gateway_id": "..."
  }
}

```
**Configuration Verified:**
- `plugins/config.yaml` contains WebhookNotification plugin (lines 983-1036)
- Webhook URL: `http://localhost:9999/webhook`
- Events: `["violation", "tool_success", "tool_error", "rate_limit_exceeded", "pii_detected"]`
- Authentication: `type: "none"`
- Enabled: `true`

---

### 🧠 Environment Info (if manual testing)

| Key              | Value                        |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Gateway version  | `main` latest          |
| Python version   | `3.11`                  |
| Transport tested |`http` (via `/servers/{server_id}/mcp`)  |
| OS / Platform    | `Ubuntu` (WSL2 on Windows 11)         |
| Container        | `none` (direct Python execution)    |
| Server mode      | Tested with both `make serve` (gunicorn) and `make dev` (uvicorn) |

**Additional Environment Details:**
- `.env` has `PLUGINS_ENABLED=true` (verified)
- `plugins/config.yaml` exists and is valid YAML
- Plugin file exists: `plugins/webhook_notification/webhook_notification.py`
- Redis disabled (not required for webhook plugin)
- Authentication working (JWT tokens valid)
> If applicable (ex: new type of test) add information on how to set this up using CI/CD with GitHub Actions or contribute directly to the workflow in `.github/workflows`

---

### 📎 Related PRs / Issues (optional)
https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/issues/2489

**Potential Root Causes:**
1. Plugin manager factory initialization failing silently
2. `lifespan()` function not completing plugin initialization
3. Environment variable not being read correctly by plugin framework
4. Plugin YAML parsing or validation error not being logged

**Investigation Needed:**
- Add debug logging to `init_plugin_manager_factory()` call
- Verify `settings.plugins.enabled` value at runtime
- Check if exception is being caught and suppressed during plugin init
- Confirm `get_plugin_manager()` is being called and returning non-None

comments.author: bogdanmariusc10
comments.body:
Hello, @vcostin-dev ! Thanks for the detailed bug report! After investigating, this is **not a bug** - the webhook notification plugin is working as designed but needs configuration changes to function.

## Root Cause

The WebhookNotification plugin is explicitly **disabled** in your configuration file.

**File:** `plugins/config.yaml`  
**Line 1001:**
```yaml
mode: "disabled"
```

When a plugin's mode is set to `"disabled"`, it won't execute any hooks even when the plugin subsystem is enabled.

## How to Fix

### 1. Enable the Plugin Mode

Edit `plugins/config.yaml` line 1001:

```yaml
# Change from:
mode: "disabled"

# To one of these modes:
mode: "sequential"    # Block on violations/errors (production)
mode: "transform"     # Log only, don't block (monitoring)
```

**📚 Documentation:** See [Plugin Execution Modes](https://ibm.github.io/mcp-context-forge/using/plugins/#execution-modes) for details on each mode.

### 2. Configure Your Webhook Endpoint

Update the webhook configuration (lines 1007 and 1021):

```yaml
webhooks:
  - url: "http://localhost:9999/webhook"  # Your test receiver
    events:
      - "violation"
      - "tool_success"
      - "tool_error"
      - "rate_limit_exceeded"
      - "pii_detected"
    authentication:
      type: "none"
    retry_attempts: 2
    retry_delay: 1000
    timeout: 10
    enabled: true  # Change from false
```

### 3. Restart the Gateway

```bash
make dev
```

## Expected Behavior After Fix

1. Gateway startup will show: `"Plugin manager initialized with X plugins"`
2. Tool invocations will trigger the `tool_post_invoke` hook
3. Webhook HTTP POST will be sent to `http://localhost:9999/webhook`
4. Your receiver will display the notification payload

## Why the Log Was Missing

The log message `"Plugin manager initialized with X plugins"` only appears when:
- The plugin subsystem is enabled (`PLUGINS_ENABLED=true`)
- The shared plugin toggle is enabled (via Redis or in-memory)
- At least one plugin manager is successfully retrieved

The plugin manager factory **does** initialize successfully (you saw "Plugin subsystem enabled"), but the manager retrieval is gated by the runtime toggle.

## Additional Resources

- **[Plugin Configuration Guide](https://ibm.github.io/mcp-context-forge/using/plugins/)** - Complete plugin setup documentation
- **[Plugin Architecture](https://ibm.github.io/mcp-context-forge/architecture/plugins/#plugin-types-and-configuration)** - Detailed explanation of plugin modes and configuration fields
- **[Webhook Notification Plugin](https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/tree/main/plugins/webhook_notification)** - Plugin-specific documentation

Let me know if you need any clarification!
